themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages in Morrisania/Crotona spiked to 15 complaints last week—a 314% increase over the 8-week baseline of 3.6 weekly complaints—raising safety and quality-of-life concerns in a district already struggling with crime-related 311 reports.
evidence: 15 street light condition complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (314% spike, z-score: 5.7)
Spike occurred in same timeframe as elevated drug activity (5 complaints last week vs. 1.5 avg) and homeless person assistance requests (5 vs. 0.8 avg)
Dark streets correlate with documented safety concerns in the district
reporting_angles: Knock on doors in blocks with the most complaints; photograph unlit streets at night; request DEP maintenance logs
Interview residents about fear, crime, and mobility impacts; connect to broader infrastructure underinvestment signals in community board budget requests

themes_detail.label: Homeless Crisis & Drug Activity Converging
themes_detail.summary: This week, homeless person assistance requests jumped 567% to 5 complaints (vs. 0.8 weekly average), while drug activity complaints rose 233% to 5 reports (vs. 1.5 weekly average), suggesting a potential convergence of unmet social services and street-level disorder.
evidence: 5 homeless person assistance complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)
5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 4.04)
Both spikes coincide with street light outages, creating perfect conditions for unpoliced open-air activity
reporting_angles: Interview outreach teams, shelter operators, and NYPD about resources; map 311 hotspots to specific blocks; talk to residents about visibility and fear
Investigate whether city social services are understaffed or overwhelmed in the district; connect to community board's long-standing park/recreation funding requests

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Spike 2 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints peaked 2 weeks ago at 25 reports—a 317% increase over the 8-week baseline of 6.0 weekly complaints—indicating possible new late-night venues, construction, or unregulated business activity in the district.
evidence: 25 commercial noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.0 weekly average (317% spike, z-score: 5.6)
Residential noise remains the top complaint category at 3,864 total over 90 days, with commercial noise now joining the pattern
No corresponding increase in DOB permits filed for new businesses, suggesting either illegal operation or enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Identify the specific blocks with highest commercial noise complaints; visit in evening/night hours; check SLA license records for new liquor licenses or violations
Interview business owners and neighbors about what changed; check city enforcement records (NYPD, DOE) for complaint response times

themes_detail.label: Animal & Sanitation Issues Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 3 weeks, unsanitary conditions tied to animals spiked 1100% (6 complaints vs. 0.5 baseline) and unleashed dog reports jumped 700% (5 vs. 0.6 baseline), both with extreme z-scores (11.0 and 5.11), signaling possible rodent or pest infestation or animal control gaps.
evidence: 6 unsanitary animal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 11.0—the highest z-score in dataset)
5 unleashed dog complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.11)
Unsanitary conditions rank 4th overall (895 complaints over 90 days), suggesting chronic sanitation infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Request Sanitation and Parks data on rodent complaints, baiting schedules, and animal control calls by block; visit sites with multiple complaints
Interview residents about visible rats, loose dogs, and uncollected trash; connect to CB's repeated requests for park renovation and upgrade funding

themes_detail.label: Infrastructure Damage Spike 3 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage spiked 3 weeks ago to 5 complaints—a 471% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.9—alongside elevated air quality complaints (3 vs. 0.5 baseline, 500% increase), suggesting possible environmental or physical degradation event.
evidence: 5 street sign damage complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 6.88)
3 air quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Both spikes suggest environmental stressor (construction dust, pollution event, or vehicle traffic increase) rather than isolated complaints
reporting_angles: Check DOB records for the 248 alteration filings over the past 90 days; identify ongoing construction projects that could cause dust/damage
Contact DEP about air quality monitoring; request Department of Transportation data on street sign damage claims
